content_voiceover: This table summarizes the phase III trial data for the three approved rebalancing agents in hemophilia, fitusiran, concizumab, and marstacimab, and it's worth comparing them side by side since boards love these head to head comparisons. Fitusiran, studied in ATLAS-OLE, targets antithrombin via siRNA and is dosed every two months, which is a major convenience advantage, but it had the highest thrombotic event count at four cases and requires monitoring of antithrombin levels specifically. Concizumab and marstacimab both target TFPI K2 as monoclonal antibodies, but concizumab is dosed daily while marstacimab is weekly with a loading dose. Concizumab's explorer trials showed very low annualized bleed rates, especially in explorer7, and notably zero thrombotic events after revised dosing, though three occurred before the protocol was adjusted. Marstacimab had one thrombotic event and requires no drug level monitoring, which simplifies use. Approval status differs too, fitusiran and concizumab are approved for patients with inhibitors, while marstacimab is approved for patients without inhibitors. Anti-drug antibody rates and adverse event profiles also vary, with fitusiran showing liver enzyme elevations and cholelithiasis, and concizumab and marstacimab showing more injection site reactions and arthralgia.
keypoints: Fitusiran targets antithrombin, dosed every two months, requires antithrombin level monitoring
Concizumab and marstacimab both target TFPI K2 but differ in dosing frequency, daily versus weekly
Fitusiran and concizumab are approved for inhibitor patients, marstacimab for non-inhibitor patients
Thrombotic events occurred with all three agents, underscoring the shared bleeding-thrombosis tradeoff
keypoint_voiceover: For boards, remember the pairing, fitusiran hits antithrombin and needs level monitoring, while concizumab and marstacimab both hit TFPI K2 but differ in approved population, inhibitor status, and dosing schedule.
